findings.title: Threat-model residual 7 misstates its own scope: the /proc/sys tunables a file tool can reach are HOST-GLOBAL, not 'of its own run', and the claim that /proc/sys is read-only for the agent's shell is not supported by the shell layer's mount flags. The residual the user accepted (D-030 option A) is therefore larger than disclosed.
findings.reproduction: Read-only assessment; no /proc/sys write was performed, as the assignment requires. (1) tools/agents/agent_sandbox.py:154-155 creates only an IPC namespace (--unshare-ipc) and binds the host procfs read-write (--bind /proc /proc). There is no user, net, UTS or PID namespace, so apart from the IPC-namespaced entries every /proc/sys entry the process-sandbox layer sees is the host kernel's single global tunable. docs/delivery/threat-model.md:60 (residual 7) instead says a file tool could write 'a /proc/sys entry of its own run'. It also says D-033 closed a 'cross-run amplification (reaching another run's /proc/<peer>/sys through /proc/<peer>/root)', but every run binds the same host /proc, so there is no per-run /proc/sys whose reach D-033 could have narrowed. The own-run framing, and the conclusion drawn from it ('availability / host-tunable risk, not repository or gate integrity'), rest on a per-run scope that does not exist. (2) threat-model.md:60 and agent_sandbox.py:149-150 say /proc/sys is 'read-only ... for the agent's shell (the Claude Code Bash sandbox's user namespace)'. In this run's own shell layer, /proc/self/mountinfo shows the topmost /proc mount as 'rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec' and the UTS namespace as the initial one (uts:[4026531838]), and access(2) reports /proc/sys/kernel/hostname writable. Any refusal there would have to come from user-namespace ownership checks, not from a read-only mount. The document does not establish that, and it cannot be confirmed without a write. Evidence: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-19/05-residual7-readonly.log.
findings.expected: Residual 7 accurately states that the reachable /proc/sys tunables are host-global (shared with the host and every concurrent run, except the IPC-namespaced entries), states what protects the shell layer (and shows it, for example by the operator running a controlled test), and bases its integrity conclusion on that real scope. The user re-confirms option A on the corrected text, or a narrower control is adopted.
findings.actual: Residual 7 describes an 'own-run' scope and a closed 'cross-run /proc/<peer>/sys amplification' that do not match the mount and namespace configuration, and asserts a read-only shell /proc/sys that the shell layer's mount flags do not show. The acceptance of F-DG0-149 as an observation is premised on this text.

history.note: Raised in round 19 by code-security-reviewer. Proposal: correct residual 7 (host-global scope; remove the '/proc/<peer>/sys amplification' claim; state and demonstrate the actual shell-layer protection), have the user re-decide D-030 option A on the corrected text, and spike a narrower control for the process-sandbox layer (for example a user namespace that does not map to host uid 0 for the claude process, or restricting file-tool writes to the role's areas at the kernel level) that keeps the reviewers' nested bwrap working.

findings.title: D-035's tolerance of a missing manifest source_commit is not limited to superseded rounds: it also applies to the gate's own round, and checkCandidate in current mode never checks gate.source_commit, so a non-existent gate source_commit passes current-mode validation
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:808-822 (findManifest) suppresses the recompute error whenever `git cat-file -e <source_commit>^{commit}` fails, for every round, including the round whose candidate is the gate candidate. The code comment and D-035 describe it as a 'superseded (non-gate) review round' tolerance. checkCandidate (rules.mjs:828-857) recomputes from the working tree in current mode and only compares manifest.source_commit with gate.source_commit (line 842), never checking that the commit exists. Reproduction in a disposable clone at 3ffb28c (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-19/r19-d035-gate-round-repro.mjs, log 01-d035-gate-round-repro.log): with the round-19 (gate) manifest's source_commit set to ffff…ffff, findManifest returns 0 errors (A1) and checkCandidate(mode=current) returns 0 errors (B). Only checkCandidate(mode=historical) rejects it (C). A reachable but wrong commit is still rejected (A2). In a stage whose findings carry no fix_revision, nothing in current mode catches it; the rules.mjs:646 ancestry check does so only indirectly.
findings.expected: The missing-commit tolerance applies only to rounds whose candidate is not the gate candidate (r.candidate_id !== gate/stage.candidate.candidate_id). Current-mode gate validation requires gate.source_commit to exist and be an ancestor of HEAD.
findings.actual: A gate record whose traceability commit does not exist passes current-mode validation. Content identity is unaffected: the working-tree recompute still binds the candidate, and historical mode, which CLAUDE.md requires before the next stage, rejects it.

history.note: Raised in round 19 by code-security-reviewer. D-035 itself, for superseded rounds, is judged an acceptable loosening of a redundant check; only its extension to the gate round is flagged. Low: content identity is preserved, and historical mode catches it.

findings.title: The candidate's project .claude/settings.json auto-allows `git push`, `git filter-branch`, `git update-ref` and `git branch`, and every agent run loads project settings, so these history-rewriting commands bypass the permission classifier for all project agents (contained by the sandbox; observation)
findings.reproduction: .claude/settings.json (commit 5a49719, 'Expand permissions in settings.json for Git commands') adds Bash(git filter-branch:*), Bash(git branch:*), Bash(git push:*) and Bash(git update-ref:*) to permissions.allow. tools/agents/run-agent.sh:184 starts every agent with --setting-sources project, so the rules apply to reviewers and implementers too. They remain contained: .git is on COMMON_DENY (agent_settings.py:34, read-only for every role), allowUnsandboxedCommands is false, and the agent shell has no network. Evidence: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-19/06-settings-allow-rules.log.
findings.expected: Allow rules needed only by the orchestrator (the D-034 history repair) live in the user's local settings (.claude/settings.local.json), which agent runs do not load, or are removed once the repair is done.
findings.actual: The rules are in project settings and part of the candidate. Defence in depth is weaker (the classifier no longer screens these commands for agents), but no write becomes possible.

history.note: Raised in round 19. Low and non-mandatory; the reporter would accept it as an observation (kernel-level containment holds), but recommends moving the rules to local settings.
